transcript:
Meeting: Pilot sync - freezepoint decision & rollback runway
Date: 2026-02-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (BrightPath Head of Data), Tom Ellis (Platform Eng), Sara Nguyen (Security)

AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY:
- Decided to propose a freezepoint of model v2.3 for immediate canary while keeping v2.1 as a fast fallback for specific latency-sensitive routes.
- Need a short rollback runway (toggle + traffic split) and an automated health-check baseline.
- Security asks clarified: KMS integration, audit log retention, and SSO mapping.

KEY TOPICS: model selection, freezepoint rationale, rollback plan, benchmarks, VPC/KMS, canary timing

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: hey everybody, thanks for joining — I see all of you, uh, appreciate you squeezing this in. We're about 45 minutes today. Quick agenda, final freezepoint recommendation, rollback runway, and then action items. Luis, do you want to start with the perf delta?
[00:22] Luis: yeah, sure. So we ran the focused 24-hour runner with the three top candidate variants — v2.1-quant, v2.3-float, and v2.3-8bit. The headline: v2.3-float gives about +8% quality on our golden prompts vs v2.1 but latency is roughly 25% higher at median. v2.3-8bit reduces that latency gap to ~10% but introduces slight hallucination uptick on domain-specific docs.
[00:55] Anika: when you say hallucination uptick, can you quantify? like false positives on diagnoses or just verbose phrasing?
[01:08] Luis: mostly hallucination is in rare entity linking — e.g., when the prompt references a historical medication name, the 8-bit path sometimes invents related but incorrect side effects. Not many, maybe 0.6% of responses in our evaluation set vs 0.2% for float.
[01:28] Tom: and cost delta? obvious question for us.
[01:32] Luis: v2.3-float is about 40% more tokens-cost on raw inference CPU/GPU hours vs v2.1 when you factor throughput and batching. v2.3-8bit is about +15% cost vs v2.1. Our batching sims show opportunity to recover some of that with continuous batching and prefix cache on repeated queries.
[01:55] Maya: quick clarifying Q for BrightPath: which routes are strictly latency-sensitive? is it the triage endpoint or the analytics batch job?
[02:06] Anika: triage. The triage path needs median < 220ms. Most of our other model-invocations are asynchronous or batched.
[02:18] Maya: good, so we probably need hybrid strategy — pin v2.3 for non-latency routes, keep v2.1 or v2.3-8bit for triage. But let's also talk rollback runway — Luis, walk us through the toggle approach.
[02:35] Luis: sure. We propose two-layer fallback: policy routing by route then a global escape hatch. Technically: Route-level pin for triage (default v2.1) and for other routes we can pin to v2.3-float. Canary: start at 2% traffic to v2.3-float with realtime SLO checks (latency P95, error rate, hallucination score based on prompt evaluation). If metric breach we flip route-level traffic to v2.3-8bit as intermediate or straight back to v2.1. Global escape hatch is an immediate config change in console to failover all traffic to v2.1.
[03:12] Tom: what's the cadence of the canary health checks? every 30s? 1m?
[03:18] Luis: default 60s, but you can configure. We recommend 60s with a 3-window rolling evaluation so we don't flip on a blip.
[03:28] Sara: on the security side, we need clarifications on KMS — is customer-managed KMS supported in sandbox? and audit logs retention for model requests?
[03:38] Maya: yes, Private deployments support customer KMS via our KMS connector (we've seen a few customers use GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault/AWS KMS). For hosted we integrate with a customer KMS in Redwood Private only, for Hosted API we provide envelope encryption but not customer-managed keys. For audit logs, we have per-request metadata and TTL; we can push logs to your S3 or GCS with a configurable retention policy.
[04:05] Sara: ok we need that on paper. send us the SOC2 scope and the exact retention options.
[04:11] Maya: will do — I'll attach the security.pdf and a short matrix.
[04:15] Anika: about rollback — what about KV cache concerns? if we drop back to v2.1, do we need to flush caches or is the KV compatible?
[04:26] Luis: good question. KV caching is model-architecture dependent. v2.3 uses a slightly different KV layout — rolling back may require cache invalidation for affected hosts. We recommend a staged invalidation: invalidate per-shard after canary rollback to avoid cold-start thundering herds. We'll put the exact command in the runbook.
[04:47] Tom: do we need cluster restarts?
[04:50] Luis: typically no restarts if you use model variant switching with the runtime — unless you change compilers or quant schemes that require different kernel sets. 8-bit variants might require a small warm-up but no full restart.
[05:03] Maya: let's go through the proposed freezepoint list. Our recommendation: freeze v2.3 as the canary candidate, v2.3-8bit as a warm-fallback, and v2.1 as the safety fallback. Any objections?
[05:15] Anika: slight hesitation — v2.3-halting was our earlier internal name; do we know of any regressions in rare prompts?
[05:22] Luis: we found two outlier prompts in the clinical set where v2.3 changed phrasing in a way clinicians flagged as ambiguous. Both are on the golden prompt list Anika will send. That's why we want the canary and a small sample evaluation window.
[05:39] Anika: ok if we can pause the canary automatically on hallucination breach then it's fine.
[05:44] Maya: yep that's standard; our health-checks include a hallucination proxy score you can define based on your rubric.
[05:50] [06:00] Speaker 1: um, sorry just to clarify, the hallucination proxy — is that computed on live traffic or on replayed golden prompts?
[06:07] Luis: both. Live traffic heuristic plus periodic replayed golden prompts sent to the canary to sample correctness. Replay frequency we recommend every 5 minutes for the canary window.
[06:17] Tom: on the infra side, we need a 2% baseline canary for one week? what's your recommendation?
[06:24] Maya: a two-week runway is safest for enterprise; but for you given the triage latency sensitivity and small traffic we can do 1 week at 2% with aggressive evaluators then expand to 10% second week if all green.
[06:34] Anika: is there a cost estimate for the canary phase? we need to attach to the pilot budget.
[06:40] Luis: for 2% traffic at v2.3-float, rough estimate is +6-8% in monthly inference spend given your traffic profile. We'll provide a better number with the 48-hour loadbench.
[06:51] Maya: quick note — the loadbench will simulate your sample traffic distribution including the triage spike patterns so the cost estimate should be accurate.
[07:00] Sara: SSO mapping — during canary will we have separate roles? we need to ensure audit trails clearly show canary requests.
[07:08] Maya: yes, we emit a route tag and a canary tag per request; those are part of the audit logs you can export. We'll add role-based filtering in the RBAC mapping so auditors can query canary traffic.
[07:20] Tom: where do we host the replay dataset? we prefer not to push clinical prompts outside our VPC.
[07:26] Maya: good point — for Private we can keep both replay and tokens within your VPC. For hosted we do encrypted transfer and ephemeral storage; but if you need full on-prem replay we can talk private deployment options.
[07:40] Anika: I think we'll try hosted first with encrypted replay — less overhead — as long as the KMS hooks meet our compliance.
[07:48] Sara: send the dataflow diagram and KMS matrix.
[07:52] Maya: will attach.
[07:55] [08:10] Luis: on rollback automation — couple technical notes: we'll implement traffic shifts via policy changes (you'll see the route config in console and via API). The runbook will contain CLI snippets to force immediate failover, a soft-fallback to 8bit, and a staged traffic sweep. We'll also include threshold values (P95 > X ms, hallucination score > Y, error rate > Z%) as triggers.
[08:35] Tom: do you publish the code for the health checks? we want to run them inside our own monitoring stack as well.
[08:40] Luis: yes, health-check probes are open and you can run them locally — they call internal evaluation endpoints we expose with an API key. We'll hand over the probe scripts.
[08:52] Anika: about golden prompts — I will finalise the 20 items and mark which are triage vs batch. Expect that by Tuesday.
[08:59] Maya: thanks. Luis, any operational TODOs we should document for them?
[09:03] Luis: I'll put the cache invalidation sequence, the per-shard invalidation command, and the warm-up snippet for 8-bit models. Also include the rollback playbook with exact metric thresholds and a sample incident timeline.
[09:15] Anika: what about fallback quality loss? how do we measure user impact if we route triage to v2.1 for a period?
[09:22] Luis: recommend A/B with a small randomized holdout and collecting downstream conversion signals (clinician override rates, triage correction rate). We'll give a sample dashboard layout.
[09:34] [10:00] Speaker 2: there was a mention earlier about a warm fallback to v2.3-8bit — are we comfortable with hallucination risk there?
[10:08] Luis: slight risk, but much lower than going straight to v2.1 for certain knowledge-heavy prompts. The idea is to preserve quality while shaving latency. It's tradeoff route-by-route.
[10:20] Tom: ok, from infra we're fine as long as KV invalidations and warm-ups are captured in the runbook and we have a script.
[10:28] Sara: please also include log retention SLA and a sample redaction approach for PHI fields. We need to ensure PII isn't stored in plaintext logs.
[10:36] Maya: we'll include our redaction patterns and field-level encryption guidance.
[10:41] Anika: last thing — timeline and sign-off. We want canary to start week of Feb 22. Does that work?
[10:48] Maya: yes. Next week we'll share the loadbench and runbook. If BrightPath signs off on the golden prompts by Tue the 16th we'll be on track.
[10:58] Tom: schedule the canary kickoff meeting and include ops runbook review.
[11:03] Maya: I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Feb 22 and invite ops + security.
[11:08] Sara: thanks all.
[11:10] Maya: okay great — recap: Maya share benchmarks + security docs, Luis share runbook, Anika finalize prompts, Tom provide infra details. Any final Qs?
[11:22] Anika: none from me.
[11:24] Tom: all good.
[11:26] Sara: good. thanks.
[11:28] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.

END TRANSCRIPT
